A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, method, experiments, and appendices A–F. All 19 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2 are readable. Text extraction and visual inspection support a reliable comparison, including confirmation of removed material.

before.justification: V1 reports original detector evaluations, style-transfer and semantic-preservation results, AURA measurements, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original detector, style-transfer, and ablation results and reports additional language-model, attack-baseline, and stylistic-representation comparisons.

M1.justification: The proposed paraphraser retains exemplar-conditioned supervised training, DPO against a classifier trained on its outputs, and iterative paraphrasing with semantic candidate selection. V2 clarifies the inference description without establishing a procedural change. AURA's removal concerns evaluation and theory.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Reddit training data, Reddit/Amazon/Blogs preference and detection datasets, and Reddit author-style-transfer evaluation. Appendix D retains the dataset statistics. Additional language models are experimental configurations, and reduced appendix breakdowns do not remove domains still evaluated in Figure 2.

E2.justification: V2 adds DIPPER and OUTFOX to the reported detection-evasion comparisons. It replaces OpenAI's detector with ReMoDetect and adds StyleDetect-CISR and StyleDetect-SD, expanding the detector set from seven to nine. DIPPER also joins the edit-distance and semantic-similarity comparisons in Table 3 and Appendix B.

E3.justification: Section 2 changes StyleDetect from one machine exemplar to an averaged embedding of 100 exemplars and adds Qwen-7B-Instruct and Mistral-Nemo-Instruct configurations. V2 removes AURA evaluation and introduces a visualization protocol using 100 Reddit outputs per attack across three embeddings. These are reported setting and evaluation-design changes; unchanged Mistral table values do not establish whether those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 expands robustness-to-optimization checks beyond Mistral-7B and adds a comparison of attack outputs across LUAR, CISR, and StyleDistance in Section 5.2/Figure 4. V1's quantitative distributional-overlap analysis is removed. The exemplar-count, paraphrase-count, and DPO ablations are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. V2's wording about 'no significant drop' is not accompanied by a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds six Qwen/Mistral-Nemo rows to Table 1, additional attack/detector curves, and DIPPER results, including average edit distance 227.40 and semantic similarity 0.84 in Table 3. Existing Mistral Table 1 values and retained Table 3 entries are unchanged. V1's AURA Table 4 disappears, and Appendix A loses its complete three-domain breakdown and results beyond 50 samples. Expanded detector comparisons do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 removes v1 Section 4, including Equations 1–2, the derivation connecting sample complexity and total variation to an overlap bound, and the formal AURA definition. This material is not relocated to an appendix or replaced by another derivation. The paraphraser's mathematical formulation remains.

C1.justification: V2 withdraws AURA as a primary contribution and removes the claims to estimating a distributional-overlap upper bound. Its abstract also narrows the recommendation against relying on machine-text detection to individual documents. The central stylistic-robustness and style-aware-paraphrasing claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds a long-tail, low-resource-author explanation for stylistic robustness and qualifies the FastDetectGPT optimization finding to models for which that detector was initially discriminative. AURA-specific interpretations of detector-class overlap disappear. The main practical limitations concerning exemplars, semantic drift, and computation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 supplies OUTFOX's prompting configuration and the StyleDistance checkpoint identifier. The release pointer changes from GitHub to an anonymous 4open.science status page, while release remains prospective in the text. Appendix C's hyperparameters and hardware, Appendix D's processing details, and Appendix F's prompts are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for OUTFOX, ReMoDetect, StyleDistance, and CISR, and removes Gretton et al.'s kernel two-sample-test reference. It also drops the claimed AURA extension of Chakraborty et al., although that work remains cited. Most related-work discussion and positioning against detector optimization and embedding-conditioned style transfer are unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized prose revisions, removes the AURA narrative, organizes experiments into numbered subsections, incorporates ablations into that section, and adds reproducibility and ethics statements. Much of the method, dataset, related-work, limitations, and appendix prose remains nearly verbatim.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figure 1, adds the three-embedding visualization, expands Table 1 and the semantic/edit-distance tables, and removes the AURA table. Detection plots receive revised legends, annotations, and sample axes. Appendix A changes from labeled three-domain panels through 200 samples to single unlabeled panels through 50, alongside substantial changes to typography and float placement.

improvement.justification: The additional Qwen/Mistral-Nemo tests, DIPPER/OUTFOX comparisons, and stylistic representations give the retained robustness and evasion claims broader empirical support. The abstract's restriction to individual-document detection also improves claim precision. The net gain is limited by removal of the quantitative overlap assessment and the complete domain-specific, longer-range detector breakdowns from Appendix A.
